descriptionChirho: Introduces the protasis of a conditional clause, marking a hypothetical or contingent situation ('if X, then Y').
Functions as a restrictive or exceptive particle limiting scope to a single alternative ('only, except, nothing but, unless').
Used in oath formulas and strong assertions to emphasize the certainty or solemnity of a statement ('surely, indeed, certainly').
Introduces a contrasting or corrective clause, often in combination with negation of the preceding statement ('but, rather, on the contrary').
Introduces a concessive clause acknowledging a condition that does not prevent the main clause outcome ('even if, although, though').
Marks a temporal condition where the conjunction introduces a time-circumstance rather than a pure hypothesis ('when, whenever').
